newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch institutional investments up in first qtr.
newsitem.headline: Dutch institutional investments up in first qtr.

text.p: The value of the large Dutch pension funds and insurers' investments portfolio grew by 13.3 percent to 933 billion guilders in the 1997 first quarter, the Central Bureau of Statistics said on Thursday.
The pension funds' total portfolio value increased by 12 percent to 622.3 billion guilders and the large insurance groups realised year-on-year growth of 16 percent to 310.7 billion.
The CBS said the trend to put more money in shares and bonds, which are more liquid than other investment forms, had continued in the first quarter of this year.
Pension funds and insurers' holdings in shares had a total value of 280.2 billion guilders at end-March 1997, up 33.4 percent from 210 billion in the year-ago period.
Investments in bonds totalled 273 billion guilders, an increase of 25.3 percent compared with the 217.8 billion posted in the first three months of 1996.

Property holdings and investments in mortgage loans grew slightly but privately placed loans now totalled 214.8 billion guilders, down 10.6 percent from 240.3 billion in the first quarter of last year.
